parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Most of PlaceOrderUseCase.ts fits the application layer. It loads products through repository ports, delegates the stock check and reservation to the domain StockManager service, saves through the OrderRepository port and maps the result to a DTO.

However, execute() also enforces business invariants of the Order aggregate itself: an order must have at least one line, and each line quantity must be positive. These rules belong in the domain layer, in the Order entity's constructor or factory, or in a domain service. In this file they sit in the use case, so the Order entity can be built in an invalid state when called from any other path. That is domain knowledge leaking into the application layer.

A secondary issue: generateOrderId() calls Date.now() and Math.random() directly to create identities. That is a technical concern better hidden behind an ID-generator port that infrastructure implements, though this is a smaller point.

Checking that a product exists, by contrast, is reasonable application-level orchestration.
